subject: License vs consumption: packaging options & quantization guidance for Optimize toolkit
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: License vs consumption: packaging options & quantization guidance for Optimize toolkit

Priya / Anand —

Thanks again for the thoughtful run-through on Friday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short note with two concrete packaging paths and the technical guardrails our Optimize toolkit team recommends so you can compare costs and operational effort quickly. High level: one is license-first (reserved/dedicated capacity + Optimize toolkit add-on) and the other is consumption-first (hosted API + usage-based Optimize credits).

Quick bullets so you can share internally:
- License-first (Dedicated): predictable monthly spend; best for high steady throughput (>= 50M tokens/mo). Adds a smaller per-token delta once committed; includes extended observability and dedicated KV cache.
- Consumption-first (Hosted + credits): lower up-front, elastic for bursts; Optimize credits reduce effective per-token cost by enabling batching/caching/quantization recommendations and a quota of pre-warmed instances.

Questions I want to answer for you: typical effective $/1k tokens under each model for your expected workload, the recommended quantization profile for your model family, and a mutual action plan to validate quality regressions with our eval harness. If you can confirm the monthly token estimate range (rough number is fine) and whether you need data residency, I’ll attach a comparison and a draft term sheet.

I’ve looped in Laura for procurement/legal scoping. We can turn this into a 2-week eval (benchmarks + production-like pilot) if you want — Jordan can provide quantization/latency tradeoffs for the specific generator you mentioned.

Next step: reply with the token range and any constraints (SLA, compliance) and I’ll push an adjusted comparison.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: packaging-comparison.xlsx (summary), technical-appendix.pdf (benchmarks & quant notes)

Ben —

Thanks, helpful framing. A few clarifying items before we ask procurement to look at the term sheet:

1) Monthly token estimate: range is 8–18M tokens/month today, projected to 35–60M in 6–9 months if adoption ramps as expected.
2) Residency: US only is fine for now.
3) Quality sensitivity: we cannot tolerate >1.5% change in top-level generation accuracy (we run a 400-case prompt set for regressions).

Specific asks:
- Can you show projected effective $/1k tokens for both models at 10M, 30M, and 60M tokens/mo?
- What quantization profiles do you recommend for our base model (gpt-3.5x analog) to balance latency vs quality?
- If we take a short (2-week) evaluation, what levers are included in the Optimize credits vs things we'd need to configure in Dedicated capacity?

Happy to set a quick 30-min call but if you can send the numbers and the draft term sheet we’ll start internal review.

Priya — thanks for the clear asks. I’ve attached a short compare (packaging-comparison.xlsx) and a draft term sheet (draft-term-sheet.docx). Highlights below — I’ll let Jordan add the technical detail on quantization.

Projected effective $/1k tokens (rough, includes Optimize credit impact where applicable):
- At 10M tokens/mo: License-first: $34/1k (after commit); Consumption + Optimize credits: $52/1k (with baseline credit amortization)
- At 30M tokens/mo: License-first: $22/1k; Consumption + credits: $30/1k
- At 60M tokens/mo: License-first: $16/1k; Consumption + credits: $21/1k

Notes:
- License-first assumes a 12-month reserved pool with a 15% discount on list for the Dedicated SKU. It also assumes we enable KV cache sharing for your use case which reduces per-token compute on repeated prefixes (we’ve seen 20–35% token-savings on similar retrieval-augmented workflows).
- Consumption path uses Optimize credits to buy down the per-token cost for the pilot window; credits cover recommended pre-warm and adaptive batching config as well as quantization advisory. Credits are consumed during the pilot and then converted into per-token discounts for any committed consumption plan if you convert.

Attachments: packaging-comparison.xlsx, draft-term-sheet.docx

I’ve proposed a 2-week eval window in the term sheet: Redwood provides a sandbox with the Optimize toolkit enabled, 100k credits pre-funded for experimentation, and a lightweight telemetry pack so you can run your 400-case prompt suite. If quality holds (<=1.5% regression), we move to either a Consumption conversion with committed credits or finalize a Dedicated quote.

Jordan — can you add the recommended quant profile and expected latency hit for LetterWave’s generator?

—
Ben

On 2026-05-24 08:05, Ben Carter wrote:
> Jordan — can you add the recommended quant profile and expected latency hit for LetterWave’s generator?

Priya / Ben — quick technical note from the runtime/Optimize team. Short version: safe quant profile we recommend is FP16 -> INT8 (dynamic range-aware) with per-layer calibration and selective higher-precision for the last decoder layers. That gives the following ballpark tradeoffs based on our internal benchmarks for GPT-3.5x analogs:

- FP16 baseline: latency 1.0x, quality delta 0%
- INT8 (calibrated): latency ~0.6x–0.75x, expected quality regression ~0.3%–0.9% depending on prompt distribution; for your 400-case suite we estimate ~0.5% median impact.
- Mixed (INT8 except last 2 layers FP16): latency ~0.7x, quality regression ~0.15% median — recommended for your quality envelope.

Batching & cache guidance:
- Enable adaptive batching with a soft cap to keep 95th percentile latency under your SLA; we suggest an initial target of 180–220ms p95 for generation.
- KV prefix caching for repeated context: expect 15–30% token compute reduction depending on prefix reuse.

Operational notes for the eval:
- The 100k Optimize credits included in the sandbox will be consumed by pre-warm instances and by the autoscaler warming we need to measure steady-state tail latency. We’ll instrument the eval harness so you can map credit consumption to effective $/1k tokens in the spreadsheet.
- If you choose Dedicated, we can bake the mixed-precision profile into the model bundle we deploy and include a small runbook for fallbacks (auto-rollover to FP16 last-2-layers if model drift triggers a quality-alert).

Happy to sync for 20 mins with your ML infra team to walk the calibration steps; I can send a short runbook after the call.

—
Jordan Blake
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
